reports.headline: CONTINUED Failure to Address SCU Wandering/Aggression Risk in Service Plans

paragraphs.text:
CONTINUED Failure to Address SCU Wandering/Aggression Risk in Service Plans
A follow-up survey to a 3/4/2026 complaint investigation found the residence continued to fail to accurately reflect safety interventions on service plans for 3 of 4 Special Care Unit (dementia/memory care) residents, despite all SCU residents wearing wanderguard monitors for exit-seeking risk. Progress notes documented an escalating pattern the service plans never incorporated: one resident repeatedly attempting to exit the unit; another with documented altercations including trying to push a walker into another resident (intercepted by that resident's hands) and, separately, grabbing/hitting another resident's arm during a verbal altercation, plus multiple episodes of aggression toward staff (grabbing a staff member's wrist, yelling, refusing to relinquish a butter knife, requiring a hospital send-out for a mental status change). This was cited as a repeat/continued deficiency from the prior survey.

Kitchen Sanitation (Continued)
Continued food-code violations: dust accumulation on kitchen exhaust fans, trash receptacles with damaged (holed) lids, and food prep without a hair restraint.

reports.headline: CONTINUED Failure to Update Assessments/Service Plans for Outside Services

paragraphs.text:
CONTINUED Failure to Update Assessments/Service Plans for Outside Services
A follow-up survey to a 3/12/2026 complaint investigation found the residence continued to fail to update comprehensive assessments and service plans to reflect outside skilled-nursing (wound care) and physical-therapy start/end-of-care dates for 2 of 3 residents reviewed.

CONTINUED Certified Food Safety Manager Coverage Gaps
Continued failure to have a manager certified in food safety present during preparation of hot potentially-hazardous foods on 7 separate dates in May-June 2026, despite this being a repeat citation.

Quality Assurance
QA committee met only twice in approximately a year (July and October 2025), not quarterly as required. No quality improvement plan existed.

Safe Resident Handling Program
Facility with an Alzheimer's/Dementia Special Care Unit license had no Safe Resident Handling program of any kind — no committee, no written program, no policy, no hazard assessment, no annual evaluation.

Assessments Not Updated
Resident #1's assessment was not updated to reflect new wound care services or a scabies diagnosis. Resident #2's assessment was not updated to reflect physical therapy services. Scabies diagnosis not documented in care record; wound care and PT not reflected in assessments.

Service Plans Not Updated
Resident #1's service plan lacked wound care documentation and infection control interventions following a scabies diagnosis. Resident #2's plan did not reflect PT services.

Food Safety Manager Coverage
Both certified FSMs were simultaneously absent for weeks (2/19–3/4/26). No FSM was present during hot food preparation on at least eight dates. Multiple weeks without required food safety oversight.

CMT Evaluations Not Conducted
Required monthly and quarterly performance evaluations were missing for all five Certified Medication Technicians reviewed, across multiple years of employment.

Medications Without Directions for Use
Eleven medications on cart D and one on cart A/B lacked required directional labels, including Tylenol, stool softeners, vitamins, and supplements. Acknowledged by staff during survey. Significant medication error risk across multiple carts.

LHS Without Physician Orders
Two residents with suprapubic catheters were receiving limited health services without the required physician's order authorizing the facility to provide that care.

LHS Residents Not Informed of Outside Provider Rights
Same two residents were never informed in writing of their right to receive LHS care from an outside home nursing or hospice agency.

No Physician on QA Committee
As an LHS-licensed facility, a physician, NP, or PA is required as a QA Committee member. None attended.

reports.headline: Residents Retained Without Required Secure Memory Care

paragraphs.text:
Residents Retained Without Required Secure Memory Care
2 residents needing a secure memory care unit (facility not licensed to provide one) were retained. Resident #1 (severe cognitive impairment, numerous falls) eloped through a back door and was found by police outside at night, naked and soaked in urine, in a wheelchair in the street, saying she was trying to escape/go to a Friars game. Resident #2 (severe dementia) threw metal utensils and a knife during a dining-room outburst that narrowly missed another resident's head; police/EMS were called, and the resident required a private 24/7 aide until transfer to a secure memory-care facility.

Resident Records
2 residents had inaccurate records: one resident's allergy (cat dander) was omitted from the comprehensive assessment (listed "NKA"); another resident's advance directive was inconsistently documented as both CPR and DNR across different records, and multiple medication doses were refused/missed without physician notification, including a stretch where the resident was hospitalized and the MAR miscoded the admission dates.

Assessments & Service Plans Not Updated for Behaviors/Elopement Risk
Same findings as S310 — the escalating falls, wandering, elopement, and aggression documented in progress notes for both residents were never reflected in their comprehensive assessments or service plans, despite ongoing decline (BIMS scores dropping to severe impairment) and repeated safety incidents.

Annual In-Service Training
Staff A (LPN, hired 2018) had documentation of only one non-required training topic for the year. Staff B (LPN, hired 2024) had no documentation of any required 2025 in-service trainings. Administrator acknowledged both were out of compliance

reports.headline: Treatments Without Physician Orders Most serious

paragraphs.text:
Treatments Without Physician Orders Most serious
Resident #1 (COPD) was receiving oxygen set at 3L on the concentrator but believed she received 2L — no physician order for oxygen existed. Resident #2 (Type 2 diabetes) had blood sugars documented twice weekly with no physician order; values of 598 and 600 (normal 70–100) were never communicated to the physician. Resident harm: Resident #1 receiving incorrect oxygen dose without oversight; Resident #2 with critically elevated blood sugars with no physician notification.

Resident Records
Resident #1's medication list had not been updated since move-in (January 2025); when hospitalized in November for altered mental status, toxicology showed benzodiazepine, fentanyl, and opiates — none on the facility's medication list. Hospital noted no medication list was received on transfer. Resident #2 had no physician order for finger sticks, multiple dates with no values recorded, and abnormal readings never communicated to the physician. Resident harm: inaccurate medication records contributed to incomplete hospital transfer and unmonitored dangerous blood sugar levels.

Inaccurate Resident Assessments
Assessments for both residents did not accurately reflect care needs. Resident #1 assessed as not using OTC medications and lacking cognitive ability to self-administer medication — yet was observed with OTC medications in room and self-administering oxygen. Resident #2's assessment inaccurately reflected self-administration when full staff assistance was required.

Inaccurate Service Plans
Service plans for both residents did not match actual care needs or physician orders. Resident #1's plan did not reflect oxygen therapy or OTC medications. Resident #2's plan referenced physician-ordered blood sugar checks but no such order existed.

Unsecured Medications Most serious
Following a hospitalization for a possible suicidal attempt, Resident #1 was found with multiple unsecured, unordered medications in her room including an inhaler, muscle rub, antibiotic cream, pain gel, and Biofreeze. No active physician orders existed for any of them. Resident Care Director acknowledged the resident was not supposed to have medications in her possession after the hospitalization. Resident harm: resident with recent possible suicidal attempt had unsecured unordered medications accessible in her room.

Safe Resident Handling Committee
No safe resident handling committee existed despite being required under the facility's limited health services license. Resident Care Director acknowledged the deficiency.

Employee Training
Three new employees (Staff A, B, C — hired April–August 2025) had no documentation of required food service training within 30 days of hire.

Survey Results Not Posted
Most recent state licensing survey results were not prominently displayed in the lobby as required. Resident Care Director acknowledged this during interview.

Food Code Violations
Multiple violations observed 10/14–10/15/25: unlabeled/undated refrigerated food; a dietary aide who wiped hands on clothing instead of washing after handling soiled dishes; multiple food items above required cold holding temperature; a cook who wiped a thermometer with a dirty dishtowel before inserting it into ready-to-serve pasta; and cleaning chemicals stored next to food and utensils. Resident harm: residents served food at unsafe temperatures prepared under unsanitary conditions.

Fire Extinguisher Inspections
Extinguishers on multiple floors had not been inspected monthly as required by facility policy and state regulation. Director of Maintenance acknowledged the deficiency.

Physician on QI Committee
No licensed physician, NP, or physician assistant on the Quality Improvement Committee as required for limited health services licensure. QI plan also missing required LHS-related topic areas.

Employment Health Screenings
Three staff members (hired 2003, 2008, and 2018) lacked documentation of required pre-employment immunization screenings for MMR, Varicella, TDAP, and Hepatitis B. Resident harm: residents receiving limited health services potentially exposed to staff never screened for communicable diseases.

Comprehensive Assessment Completed by Unauthorized Staff
A new resident's admission comprehensive assessment was completed and signed by an LPN rather than the required registered nurse; Administrator acknowledged the staff member (Nurse Manager) is an LPN and therefore not authorized to complete assessments.

Resident-to-Resident Sexual Abuse Not Reported/Addressed
RIDOH received a report that a memory-care resident (with documented sexually inappropriate behaviors toward staff earlier that month) placed another resident's hand on his/her own groin area. Facility failed to report an earlier, related unwitnessed incident between the same two residents (5/26/2026, on a bus, where the second resident showed visible distress and asked not to sit with the first resident again) to RIDOH as required. Despite the warning signs, a surveyor observed the two residents sitting next to each other on a couch on 6/12/2026, and the Administrator could not show interventions were being followed to protect the second resident from further sexual behavior. The perpetrating resident was ultimately issued a 30-day termination notice and involuntarily discharged on 7/11/2026 (over the State Ombudsman's appeal), after the operator refunded the resident's security deposit to secure family agreement to fund a private one-on-one sitter in the interim.

reports.headline: Service Plans Not Updated for Known Aggression; Resident Struck With a Chair

paragraphs.text:
Service Plans Not Updated for Known Aggression; Resident Struck With a Chair
For 4 of 5 residents reviewed, service plans failed to reflect documented aggressive/altercation behaviors and needed interventions. RIDOH received a report that a resident (alleged perpetrator, documented as confrontational, verbally aggressive, and threatening toward staff/other residents) walked up to another resident, was verbally abusive, then followed and struck the victim with a chair. The alleged perpetrator's service plan had not been updated with interventions despite a documented pattern of altercations, and a separate resident's service plan failed to address interventions for a resident with a history of falls (5 falls between January and March 2026).

Infection Control / Scabies Outbreak Mismanaged
Facility had a confirmed scabies case; only the resident's roommate was treated prophylactically (other residents/staff were not), and staff used apple cider vinegar to disinfect surfaces exposed to scabies — not a CDC-recommended method — with the Administrator unable to provide any facility scabies protocol.

paragraphs.text: S415: Roommate was helping a resident dress, transfer, and use the toilet / A hospital social worker reported a resident's decline. The resident's roommate told the surveyor s/he helps the resident with dressing, getting out of bed, and toileting. The Director of Nursing did not know the resident needed help, and the service plan still listed the resident as independent or needing only supervision.

S330: No 30-day written notice of a rate increase / A resident whose Social Security the residence manages as payee got a notice of a 2.8% room and board increase that gave no dollar amounts, and did not get the required 30-day written notice.

S 300 — Residency Agreement/Inappropriate Placement
The facility retained a resident whose needs exceeded what an assisted living setting could safely provide. The resident had a diagnosis of major depressive disorder and was prescribed Vynase (a Schedule II stimulant the facility cannot administer). The resident had a bottle of acetaminophen in her room without a physician order, and staff were unaware. Records showed the resident had previously been found wandering a beach in Massachusetts, tested positive for cannabis and amphetamines, and had multiple knives and unprescribed medications in her room. The State had cited the facility for this same resident's safety on 9/5/2025 and it was recommended she be transferred to a secure unit — yet the facility re-admitted her. Serious finding: A resident with documented dangerous behaviors, substance use, wandering, and medication safety concerns — flagged by the state just weeks earlier — was re-admitted despite safety concerns. The Administrator herself acknowledged the resident was not in an appropriate living arrangement.
S 560 — Medication Services (Schedule II)
A medication aide was administering Vynase (a Schedule II controlled substance) to the same resident from 8/16/2025 through 9/30/2025, which is prohibited at an M1 assisted living facility. The pharmacist had notified the facility it could not administer this medication, yet it continued. Serious finding: An unlicensed medication aide was dispensing a Schedule II narcotic in violation of state law for over six weeks after the facility was told to stop.

reports.headline: S 230 — Standard of Care/Inappropriate Placement (two residents)

paragraphs.text:
S 230 — Standard of Care/Inappropriate Placement (two residents)
Two residents were determined to be inappropriately placed in a traditional assisted living setting:

Resident #1 (schizophrenia): Received the wrong dose of Clozapine (an antipsychotic) — 100 mg instead of the ordered 200 mg — from 7/8/2025 through 8/1/2025 due to physician orders not being followed. Resident sent to a higher level of care as a result of the medication error.
Resident #2 (memory loss and seizures): Was moved from a secured memory care unit to an unsecured traditional assisted living unit without a physician order documenting this was safe and appropriate.
Resident #3 (major depressive disorder with psychotic features): Was found wandering a beach in Massachusetts, found with multiple knives and drugs in her room, and tested positive for cannabis and amphetamines at the hospital. The facility failed to contact the physician regarding the resident being found out of state, and failed to document the appropriateness of her placement.

Darlington Assisted Living had the same resident (#3) flagged in both the 9/5/2025 and 10/22/2025 surveys — and re-admitted her between them despite documented safety concerns.

Written quality improvement plan did not include all required components — specifically failed to address medication administration errors and resident falls.
S 170 – Administrative Management (Staffing)
Two PCAs (Staff A and B) were providing hands-on personal care (bathing, dressing, showering) without holding active Rhode Island CNA licenses. Administrator acknowledged PCAs do not hold active RI CNA licenses. Serious deficiency — unlicensed staff providing personal care. Facility immediately ceased assigning PCAs to personal care tasks.
S 295 – Smoking Policy
Facility failed to complete smoking assessments upon admission and quarterly for two smoking residents (IDs #1 and #2). Resident ID #1 (COPD) was observed smoking outside in an undesignated area (behind building near a bench) at 7:30 AM. Cigarette butts confirmed the violation. Resident ID #2 had no initial smoking assessment and no quarterly assessments documented.
S 335 – Resident Records
Facility failed to include outside agency occupational therapy service notes in the medical record of Resident ID #3 (history of TIA). The DOW could not provide evidence of outside agency notes.
S 400 – Nurse Review
Nurse reviews for all 6 sample residents were missing required components, including: time of assessment, physical assessment, appropriateness of placement, and/or medication regimen monitoring. Multiple missed reviews also identified (e.g., Resident ID #1 missing April 2025 review; Resident IDs #5 and #6 missing December 2024/2025 reviews).
S 405 – Service Plans
Service plans for smoking residents (IDs #1 and #2) did not include smoking-specific interventions or accurate safety expectations. Resident ID #1's plan was not updated annually and didn't reflect elopement-related smoking risk.
S 560 – Dietetic Services
Multiple food safety violations: expired canned goods (chili con carne, best by 8/21/2025, including a dented can), food without labels or use-by dates, grease/debris buildup on equipment (panni maker, stove), uncovered trash containers, cell phones stored in kitchen, cleaning chemicals near food, and brooms stored improperly.
S 635 – Medication Aide Evaluations
Facility failed to conduct required monthly (first 3 months) and quarterly evaluations for 5 of 5 CMTs reviewed (Staff C, D, E, F, G). Multiple evaluation periods were entirely missing.
S 640 – Medication Storage/Administration
Medication cart inspection on 1/15/2026 found: multiple medications without directions for use (Metamucil, fiber supplement, Vitamin D, aspirin), an opened undated Lantus insulin pen (discard 28 days after opening), missing PRN medications (Ondansetron and Meclizine for Resident #4, Lidocaine patch for Resident #5), and acetaminophen/famotidine labels not matching physician orders. Significant medication management failure across multiple residents.

reports.headline: Residency Requirements / Secure Memory Care Needed but Not Provided

paragraphs.text:
Administrative Management / Medication Order Delay
An RN suggested increasing a resident's PRN pain medication dosage/frequency, but a delayed written order from the medical provider meant the resident held the PRN as previously ordered until the day of the survey.

Residency Requirements / Secure Memory Care Needed but Not Provided
A resident with anoxic brain injury (facility not licensed for secure memory care) had 4 successful elopements (2019, 2022, 11/2025, and 5/29/2026 — found at 2:17 AM trying to enter a building, returned by local police); the resident's GPS tracker watch was malfunctioning and not holding a charge.

Resident Records
Hospice provider visit notes were missing from the resident's record; had to be obtained from the outside provider at the surveyor's request.

Comprehensive Assessment Incomplete
A resident who self-administers narcotic pain medication never had the required self-administration-of-medication assessment completed.

reports.headline: Management of Services / Therapeutic Diets Not Served

paragraphs.text:
Management of Services / Therapeutic Diets Not Served
Facility failed to follow physician-ordered therapeutic diets ("no concentrated sweets," "no added salt") for 2 residents — staff confirmed no special diets are actually served, all residents get the same meal. A separate resident was found self-administering multiple OTC medications (Cortizone, Neosporin, antibiotic cream, eye drops, Loperamide) at bedside despite no order to self-administer; the DNS was unaware the resident had meds at bedside or that therapeutic diets weren't being provided.

Medication Services / Insecure Storage
Same over-the-counter medications at bedside represented insecure medication storage, acknowledged by the Director of Nursing Services as improper.

S 385 – Resident Assessment
Annual comprehensive assessments were incomplete for all 4 residents reviewed (IDs #1–4). Section Six (Medication Administration) was not completed. Additionally, Resident ID #2's smoking status was not reflected in the annual assessment.
S 400 – Nurse Review
Nurse reviews for all 4 residents reviewed lacked required components: medication regimen monitoring, physician order review, recommendations, physical assessment, and medication verification. Resident ID #2 also lacked evidence of 90-day nurse reviews being completed consistently.
S 405 – Service Plans
Service plans for all 4 residents lacked required components including description of all services, parties responsible, and interventions. Notably, Resident ID #1 had three prior elopements (11/26/2019, 8/9/2022, 11/2/2025) and the service plan failed to include elopement-prevention interventions. Resident ID #2's plan did not reflect smoking status or safety interventions.

reports.headline: Resident Found Unresponsive, Presumed DNR Without Checking; Died

paragraphs.text:
Resident Found Unresponsive, Presumed DNR Without Checking; Died
Staff found a resident unresponsive after lunch and assumed — without checking — that the resident was Do Not Resuscitate; the resident was actually full code. Staff did not perform CPR and did not call 911 promptly; both staff members involved later said they did not know the resident's actual code status. The facility also had no written advance-directives policy giving staff clear instructions for medical emergencies.
This happened amid a broader pattern of neglected oversight: a separate resident was self-administering oxygen with no physician's order; all four sample residents' comprehensive assessments had not been reviewed in four to seven years — not since their original admission — and none of the four had a nurse review completed as required; medications on a cart were expired, unlabeled, and stored insecurely; and fire drill records did not document who had conducted each drill.

paragraphs.text: S640: Insulin pen undated and one iron bottle shared by two residents / A resident's opened insulin pen had no date (it must be discarded 28 days after opening). One unlabeled bottle of ferrous sulfate was being shared between two residents instead of each having a pharmacy-labeled supply. Discontinued medications were still on the cart for another resident.

S560 and S580: Kitchen food safety and no certified food manager on 17 days / Soup, ground pot roast, and mashed cauliflower were 5 to 6 days past their discard dates, beef was thawing in standing water, and food was unlabeled. On 17 days in January 2026 no certified food safety manager was on duty while hot food was prepared.
S540: No infection control protocols for transfers / Infection control policies had no protocols for transferring or discharging residents with infections such as MRSA, C. diff, or tuberculosis.

S 380 – Resident Assessment
Facility failed to complete an adequate initial assessment for Resident ID #1 (Alzheimer's), which did not capture the resident's wandering history from prior independent living placement. The resident was an elopement risk and the facility does not hold a secure special care unit license. Administrator acknowledged the resident's needs exceeded the facility's licensure level. Serious safety concern — elopement risk resident placed in non-secure facility.
S 450 – Elopement Reporting
Resident ID #1 eloped on 11/5/2025 and police were called by a family member, not the facility. The RI Department of Health was not notified within 24 hours as required. Serious deficiency — failure to report police-involved elopement.
S 460 – Incident Investigation
Facility failed to thoroughly investigate an allegation of staff-to-resident abuse involving Staff A (CNA) against Resident ID #2, reported 11/4/2025. The internal investigation did not include: interviews with other residents about their care from Staff A, interviews with staff about any abuse of other residents, or review of a prior 12/22/2022 abuse allegation against the same staff member. No corrective actions were put in place after the 2022 incident, despite a final warning being issued at that time. This is a serious pattern-of-abuse deficiency.

S 370 – Resident Assessment (Post-Hospitalization)
Resident ID #1 (vascular dementia) was hospitalized 7/10/2025 for falls and returned 7/16/2025. The comprehensive assessment was last completed 5/21/2025 and was never updated within 5 working days of readmission as required.
S 490 – Dietetic Services
Hair/beard restraint violations observed on both 10/15 and 10/16/2025 (multiple dietary staff without proper restraints). Equipment cleanliness issues: grill pan, stove corners, pan rack, shelving with grease/debris accumulation. Freezer flaps with ice accumulation, chest freezer with bread stored amid frost. Uncovered trash containers in dish room and cook's area.

Two of three new employees reviewed (Staff B, hired 9/4/2025 as a NA; Staff C, hired 10/23/2025 as a CMT) did not receive the required 2 hours of orientation/training within 10 days of hire and prior to working alone. Required topics including fire prevention, abuse recognition, elopement procedures, and infection control were not documented as completed.

S 640 – Medication Storage
Two medication carts had medications stored insecurely: an opened, undated Lantus Solostar insulin pen (manufacturer requires discard 28 days after opening) and an opened, undated Trelegy Elipta inhaler (manufacturer requires discard 6 weeks after opening). Potential resident safety risk from expired/degraded medications.

S 375 – Nurse Review
Resident ID #1 is prescribed Methadone (Schedule II controlled substance) administered at an off-site clinic daily. The nurse review dated 7/16/2025 did not reflect monitoring of the Methadone regimen's frequency and the resident's clinic visit schedule. Staff A (LPN) was unaware daily administration was required and that the resident was self-administering at the residence. Schedule II controlled substance monitoring failure.
S 430 – Incident Investigation (Reporting)
A residence-reported incident (10/12/2025) revealed Resident ID #1 had 14 bottles of Methadone stored in their room. The facility failed to thoroughly investigate: no physician order for self-administration was on file, no evidence of secured storage, and the Administrator was unaware of the stockpile. controlled substance stockpiling not investigated.
S 565 – Medication Administration

reports.headline: Assessments & Service Plans Not Updated for Behaviors

paragraphs.text:
Assessments & Service Plans Not Updated for Behaviors
For all 6 residents reviewed (memory care), comprehensive assessments and service plans failed to be updated to reflect escalating behaviors and outside services (PT/OT start/end dates). Progress notes over months documented increasingly severe aggression (throwing/attempting to throw walkers at staff and residents, punching threats, banging on emergency exits attempting to elope) and repeated sexually disinhibited behavior between cognitively impaired residents — including being found nude/partially clothed together in showers, one resident's hands under another's shirt/on their chest, and "consensual" designations applied without any documented capacity-to-consent assessment.

Assessment Not Updated Within 5 Days of Readmission
A resident readmitted after a hospital send-out for aggressive behavior did not have the required assessment update within 5 working days.

Reporting Requirements
Facility failed to report two incidents to RIDOH as required: a resident-to-resident incident where residents (one with Alzheimer's) were found in an intimate situation in a shower — staff decided it was "consensual" without a capacity assessment — and a second incident where a resident was found with bruising to the chest after another resident was observed with hands under her/his shirt (staff felt it didn't need to be reported because the resident "had a smile on their face").

Special Care Unit Standard of Care
Behavior-monitoring progress notes for a resident under an active order failed to describe what behavior was actually observed on 5 separate shifts. Also, in an incident involving two residents (one with hands in another's pants while a third rubbed another's private area over clothing), physicians for two of the residents involved were not notified same-day of the incident (notification was delayed).

reports.headline: Physician's Order for Secure Unit Transfer Not Followed

paragraphs.text:
Physician's Order for Secure Unit Transfer Not Followed
A resident with dementia, increasing confusion, hallucinations, and a documented safety risk had a Power of Attorney Activation Letter (6/9/2026) explicitly stating the resident needed to reside in a secured assisted living residence due to progressive dementia/cognitive impairment. As of the 7/23/2026 survey — over a month later — the resident remained in traditional (unsecured) assisted living; a surveyor observed the resident alone in his/her room partially undressed. The Executive Director could not provide evidence the physician's order for a secure-unit transfer was ever followed.

Assessments & Service Plans Not Updated for Outside Services
For multiple residents reviewed, comprehensive assessments and service plans failed to accurately reflect outside PT/OT/speech/skilled-nursing services (missing start/end-of-care dates, or documenting services never actually received).

In-Service Training
Dietary staff lacked required training on chemical hazards. A flammable oven cleaner was stored above a kitchen sink; a cook was unaware the chemicals in his department were flammable. A February 2026 laundry room fire may have been caused by kitchen rags contaminated with flammable cleaning solution. Facility fire linked to chemically-contaminated rags; staff lacked required hazard training.

Management of Services
Three ordered medications (ear wax drops, loperamide, MiraLAX) were unavailable on the medication cart for Resident #2. Additionally, Vitamin D2 50mcg was ordered but Vitamin D3 20mcg was being administered — a different supplement at a different dose. Physician had not been notified. Resident received wrong supplement at wrong dose; ordered medications unavailable.

Food Safety Manager Coverage
Food Service Manager was on leave; on 15 dates in April 2026, no RI-licensed Food Safety Manager was present during hot food preparation. One staff member on duty lacked the required certification entirely. Weeks of hot food preparation without required food safety oversight.

Medication Ordering
Resident #1's prescribed levetiracetam (anti-seizure) and Vitamin B-1 were not available in the resident's room. The resident was unaware s/he had orders for these medications. Nursing staff did not verify pharmacy deliveries against physician orders for self-administering residents. Resident with seizure disorder not receiving prescribed anti-seizure medication.

reports.headline: Unwitnessed Fall After Resident Left Unattended; Resident Died

paragraphs.text:
Unwitnessed Fall After Resident Left Unattended; Resident Died
A resident with dementia and a documented high fall risk (service plan required standby assist with walker) was being walked to the nursing station by a Nursing Assistant, who left the resident standing unattended at the station's doorway to retrieve gloves rather than seating the resident on a bench immediately outside. The resident fell, sustaining a large skin tear to the hand, facial bleeding, and bilateral blackened eyes, and died on 7/10/2026, three days after the fall. The comprehensive assessment and service plan had not been updated to reflect the resident's standby-assist need for ambulation, and the NA could not correctly describe what "standby assist" required.

paragraphs.text:
Resident Records / Allergy Discrepancies
3 residents had inconsistent allergy information across COC forms, face sheets, comprehensive assessments and physician orders (e.g., one resident's assessment omitted 4 of 5 documented allergies; another's showed "NKA" despite a documented amoxicillin allergy).

Assessments & Service Plans Not Updated (Falls, Behaviors, Outside Services, Diet Changes)
For 6-8 residents reviewed, comprehensive assessments and/or service plans were not updated to reflect falls, behavior changes, PT/OT/SLP start-and-end-of-care dates, wanderguard discontinuation, or a diet downgrade to pureed proteins; service plans also failed to name the party responsible for arranging personal care, housekeeping, laundry, and diet services for all 8 sample residents.

Resident Privacy / Old Rosters in Public Binder
The facility's publicly accessible survey binder contained resident-identifying rosters from a previously licensed nursing home operating at the site (dated 2021–2023), in addition to current ALF survey materials.

Certified Food Safety Manager Coverage Gaps

Staff administered an antibacterial ointment to Resident #1's lower back blister on 9/24, 9/25, and 9/26/2025 without a physician's order.

Comprehensive Assessments Inaccurate/Incomplete
For all 5 sample residents, comprehensive assessments did not match ADL needs documented on service plans, and several had entire sections left blank (Code Status, Current Medical Diagnoses, Psychosocial History, Dementia/Cognitive score, Medications).

Assessment Not Updated Within 5 Days of Readmission
A resident readmitted after hip-fracture hospitalization/rehab did not have the assessment updated within 5 working days.

Nurse Reviews Missing Required Components
For all 5 residents, required 90-day nurse reviews lacked a physical assessment and medication verification against physician orders.

Service Plans Missing Fall Interventions / Responsible Parties
Service plans failed to reflect fall risk with interventions despite multiple documented falls, and failed to name the party responsible for arranging care tasks, for all 5 residents.

Missing Variance Requests for Hospice
3 residents on hospice services beyond the standard timeframe lacked the required Department-approved variance.

Medication Ordering Error (Lithium)
A CMT accepted a verbal pharmacy instruction to increase a resident's Lithium from 450mg to 600mg twice daily without physician verification/reconciliation in the EMR, and administered the higher (unverified) dose; the resident developed lithium toxicity and toxic metabolic encephalopathy, was hospitalized with a supratherapeutic lithium level (2.07), and was discharged on a lower 300mg dose.

Service Plans Unsigned
Service plans for all 5 sample residents lacked required administrator and resident/responsible-party signatures.

Reporting Requirements
5-day investigation reports were not submitted to RIDOH for 2 incidents (an alleged staff-to-resident abuse allegation and a resident fall).

Limited Health Services Without Physician Order or Rights Notice
2 residents receiving suprapubic (SP) catheter care under the facility's Limited Health Services license lacked the required physician's order authorizing that care, and were never informed in writing of their right to receive that care from an outside home-nursing/hospice agency instead.

S 055 – Quality Assurance
QA plan failed to include required components for the memory care/limited health services license — specifically dementia-specific areas (pressure ulcer prevention, nutritional status, mental/psychological changes) and a plan for dietary staff shortages.
S 165 – CPR Certification
18 of 28 staff members on shift schedules did not have active CPR certification in personnel records, leaving many shifts without a certified staff member on site.
S 230 – Management of Services
Facility failed to follow physician orders for a newly admitted diabetic resident — glucose monitoring was not being performed as ordered because the resident's glucometer was at home and the residence was not performing finger sticks.
S 235 – Admission Procedures
Facility failed to comply with RI law governing electronic monitoring devices — a resident had a camera in his/her room without the required POA-signed consent form and the residence lacked required device documentation.
S 285 – Residency Requirements
One resident no longer met the definition of an assisted living resident — bedbound, incontinent, dependent on staff for eating, requiring two staff with a Hoyer lift for transfers.
S 360 – Resident Assessment
Comprehensive assessment not updated for one resident despite significant decline — became non-ambulatory, incontinent, Hoyer-lift dependent, and admitted to hospice.
S 490 – Dietetic/Food Code
Multiple violations in the main kitchen and memory care kitchenette — food held at improper temperatures, unlabeled containers, expired milk, improperly dated prepared foods, dirty refrigerator gaskets and tilt skillet, dirty ice machine chute, uncovered trash containers, and an unlabeled sanitizer spray bottle.
S 565 – Medication Services
Two medication carts had expired medications and loose unidentified pills — including expired Atropine (×2), expired Sinex nasal spray, expired eye drops, and seven loose unidentifiable pills not stored in bubble packs or vials and not linked to any resident.
S 670 – Physical Plant/Safety
Two resident room closet doors (Rooms 303 and 311) had inside locks that could not be opened from the outside with a master key, posing an entrapment risk. Most Serious: Loose unidentified pills on a medication cart, failure to perform required glucose monitoring for a diabetic resident, a resident retained beyond appropriate acuity, and lockable closet doors posing entrapment risk are the most serious findings with direct resident safety implications.

Dietetic Services (Food Code Compliance)
Based on surveyor observation, record review, and staff interview, the facility failed to comply with Rhode Island Food Code requirements in the main kitchen: utensil scoops were found stored inside the food they were used for (sugar, panko breadcrumbs, flour) rather than with handles above the food; the high-temperature dish machine's final rinse repeatedly exceeded the 194°F maximum (196–198°F recorded on multiple dates); a brown substance had accumulated on the ice machine's dispenser shield; the two condenser fans in the walk-in refrigerator had dust accumulation; and the freezer floor contained loose vegetables, packaging, and dried liquid residue.

Certified Food Safety Manager Coverage
The facility failed to ensure a manager certified in food safety was present during preparation of hot potentially-hazardous breakfast foods (eggs, egg and cheese sandwiches, bacon, sausage) on approximately 20 days between 6/12/2026 and 7/8/2026; the dietary staff member's Certified Food Protection Manager credential had lapsed and was reinstated immediately following the survey.

Fire Drill Requirements
Fire drills conducted throughout 2025 and 2026 (10 drills logged) failed to meet the requirement that at least 50% be conducted under obstructed conditions; record review and a surveyor interview with the Executive Director confirmed none of the logged drills were documented as obstructed.

paragraphs.text:
Resident Assessment/Service Plans
Facility failed to update a resident's comprehensive assessment to reflect newly started physical therapy services after a fall (1/6/26–3/5/26); the assessment reviewed after the fall did not document the outside PT services being received.

Elopement / Wandering Risk Most serious
Resident #1 (dementia, admitted September 2025) was placed on an unlocked unit. Initial assessment indicated no wandering risk, but progress notes showed repeated attempts to leave the unit beginning 9/29/25. On 10/3/25 the resident successfully eloped to a nearby hardware store and was returned by police. No care plan or interventions had been implemented prior to the elopement. Resident harm: resident with dementia eloped from an unsecured unit and was found by police, at serious risk of injury or death.

Quality Improvement Plan Incomplete
Written QI plan missing required components for the Dementia Special Care Unit: prevention/treatment of pressure ulcers, dehydration/nutritional status, and mental/psychological status changes. Also missing resident/family satisfaction and reportable incidents tracking.

Safe Resident Handling Evaluations
No quarterly safe resident handling performance evaluations completed for 3 dementia unit residents (Residents #3, #4, #5) as required by facility policy and regulation.

Resident Records: Missing Wound Documentation
Outside agency wound care notes for Resident #2 (8/20, 8/22, 8/24/25) did not include wound measurements needed to assess healing progress. Resident harm: without measurements, facility could not determine whether the wound was improving or worsening.

Service Plans Not Updated
Service plans for 3 residents not updated when new outside services began: Resident #1 (PT started 8/13/25), Resident #2 (wound care started 8/16/25), Resident #6 (ongoing twice-weekly dialysis not reflected since 2023 service plan).

Food Code Violations
Violations across kitchen and kitchenettes 8/25–8/27/25: dishwasher not reaching required sanitizing temperature; uncovered ice cube trays in two unit freezers; staff working without required hair and beard restraints; dietary aide failed to wash hands after handling soiled dishes; turkey sandwich served at 59°F (required ≤41°F). Resident harm: residents served food at unsafe temperatures under unsanitary conditions.

Bedroom Door Locks
Bedroom doors in 6 shared rooms could not be opened by master key from the outside. Staff unable to access residents in room emergencies. Resident harm: staff unable to enter locked bedrooms in an emergency.

Bathroom Door Locks
Bathroom doors in 5 rooms could not be unlocked from the outside in an emergency. Resident harm: staff unable to access residents in bathroom emergencies.

Quality Assurance Program Not Effective
Facility's QA program failed to identify causal factors or implement meaningful interventions despite falls on the memory care unit rising sharply in Q4 2025 (17 in Oct, 23 in Nov, 42 in Dec); QA meetings reviewed only one resident at a time rather than the facility-wide trend.

Reporting Requirements / Repeat Fire Incident
A humidifier filled with tap water (rather than distilled, per manufacturer guidance) and set too high caused a smoke-detector activation and fire department response; facility could not show it had checked other residents' rooms for humidifiers or educated residents on proper use to prevent recurrence.

S 285 – Residency Requirements
Facility retained a resident who no longer met the definition of an assisted living resident — the resident was bedbound, required a Hoyer lift with two staff members for transfers, and was receiving hospice services requiring a higher level of care than permitted in assisted living.
S 375 – Nurse Review
Nurse reviews for four residents failed to include required physical assessments, as evidenced by review of completed nurse review forms.
S 565 – Medication Services
Multiple medication issues across residents — a CoQ10 bottle on the cart contained 100mg when only 30mg was ordered, an opened insulin pen and inhaler were undated (manufacturer requires dating upon opening), and a medication dosage instruction for acetaminophen did not match the physician order. Staff could not provide evidence medications were properly reconciled.
S 705 – Fire Safety
Emergency floor plans were not posted on multiple floors (1st, 2nd, 4th, and 5th floors) throughout the residence.
S 730 – Variance Procedure
Facility failed to obtain required RIDOH variance approval for three residents receiving hospice and palliative care services from outside providers.
S 920 – Limited Health Services
The Quality Improvement Committee lacked a required licensed physician, certified nurse practitioner, or licensed physician assistant as a member for three consecutive quarterly meetings (January, April, and July 2025). Most Serious: Retaining a resident clearly beyond appropriate acuity for assisted living is the most serious finding. Medication dosing and reconciliation errors and failure to obtain required variances for hospice residents also represent significant compliance and safety concerns.

S 230 – Management of Services
Facility failed to follow physician orders for daily weight monitoring for a resident with congestive heart failure — multiple 3-pound single-day weight gains were not reported to the physician as ordered.
S 390 – Service Plans
Service plans not updated to reflect outside services (hospice, PT/OT) for three residents receiving those services.
S 405 – Reporting Requirements
A resident's fall resulting in hospitalization (admitted 9/12, discharged 9/16) was not reported to the Center for Health Facilities Regulation in writing by the next working day, as required.
S 535 – Housekeeping
A toilet grab bar in a resident's bathroom was not securely attached to the wall — a resident sustained a bruise to the upper left arm as a direct result. Most Serious: The unsecured grab bar causing documented resident injury is the most serious finding. Failure to report a hospitalization and failure to follow physician weight monitoring orders also represent significant lapses with direct resident harm potential.

S200 – Personnel Records
Six of six staff reviewed (A through F, including CMTs, CNAs, and an RN/Director of Wellness) lacked signed copies of the employee's awareness of resident rights. The Payroll Manager confirmed this during interview.

S380 – Resident Service Plans
Six of six residents reviewed had service plans that failed to document the description and interventions needed for their known conditions:

Resident #1 (hypertension, on mechanically altered diet, moderate fall risk with falls 11/28/24, 3/2/25, 4/20/25, 5/12/25) — service plan showed regular diet (incorrect) and no fall risk interventions.
Resident #2 (dementia, anxiety, hypertension, moderate fall risk with falls 10/7/24, 3/29/25, 5/2/25) — service plan had no fall risk interventions.
Resident #3 (dementia, anxiety, hypertension, moderate fall risk with falls 3/28/25, 4/1/25, 4/12/25, 4/26/25) — service plan had no fall risk interventions.
Resident #4 (end stage kidney disease, receiving dialysis) — service plan failed to mention dialysis treatments.
Resident #5 (BPH, nicotine dependence, urinary catheter) — service plan failed to mention the foley catheter or smoking-related interventions.
Resident #6 (congestive heart failure, using 2L oxygen via nasal cannula continuously) — service plan did not document oxygen use or safety interventions.

Fall risk residents had documented repeated falls with no care plan response — high potential for serious injury.

S555 – Medication Storage
The 6th/7th floor medication cart had an undated open Fluticasone propionate 50mcg, expired Diclofenac sodium gel (expired 1/4/2024), and expired Aspirin 81mg EC (expired 4/13/2025). The 2nd/3rd floor cart had two additional undated open Fluticasone propionate inhalers and an undated Incruse Ellipta 62.5mcg (all requiring discard 6 weeks after opening). The Director of Wellness could not confirm when any of these were opened.

S705 – Fire Drill Documentation
Fire drills conducted in 2024–2025 failed to document who conducted the drill, time taken to evacuate, employee observations of resident evacuation ability, and whether drills were obstructed. Only 2 of 8 drills (25%) were obstructed, below the required 50%. Only 1 of 8 drills was conducted during sleeping hours. The Administrator acknowledged all deficiencies.

S220 – Personnel Records
Two staff (A and B) were promoted from dietary to Nursing Assistant on 8/5/2025, but their personnel files lacked signed updated job descriptions. The Executive Director acknowledged the gap.

S250 – Management of Services / Self-Administration
Resident #1 (hypertension, receiving physical therapy since 10/10/2025) had a comprehensive assessment dated 10/16/2025 showing she lacked cognitive capacity to self-administer medications — yet no physician's order existed to self-administer her Fluticasone-Salmeterol inhaler and Albuterol. The Director of Wellness could not produce the required order.
Resident #2 (COPD, diagnosed January 2022) was self-administering a Fluticasone nasal spray, Fluticasone inhaler, and Albuterol inhaler with no physician's order for self-administration.

S390 – Resident Assessment Updates
Resident #1's comprehensive assessment (10/16/2025) showed she lacks cognitive ability to self-administer and is receiving physical therapy — but the service plan dated 11/4/2024 failed to reflect either of these facts.
Resident #3 (COPD, admitted October 2024) self-administered a Ventolin inhaler, but the comprehensive assessment dated 10/16/2025 showed the resident lacks cognitive capacity to do so. The service plan dated 10/16/2025 also failed to document this.

S415 – Service Plan Updates
For Residents #1 and #3, service plans were not updated when conditions changed significantly. Resident #1 began physical therapy 10/10/2025 with no service plan update. Resident #3's self-administration of Ventolin was not reflected in the service plan despite the cognitive capacity finding.

S560 – Dietetic Services (Kitchen)
During a 10/29/2025 observation, kitchen hood slats had heavy debris accumulation and the ice machine had black substance buildup along the inner upper right side. A trash container was uncovered when not in use. The Food Service Director acknowledged all issues and confirmed there was no established cleaning system. Potential food safety/contamination risk to all residents.

Miralax expired 7/2024
